name: Orion Nebula
tagline: The nearest stellar nursery — new suns being born in plain sight.
history: The fuzzy middle 'star' of Orion's sword resolves into the closest region of massive star formation to Earth — a cloud 24 light-years across where thousands of suns are igniting. Four young giants, the Trapezium, flood it with ultraviolet light that sculpts the glowing pillars and veils. Hubble images revealed over 150 protoplanetary disks — 'proplyds' — silhouetted inside it: solar systems in the act of assembly, direct proof that planet formation is routine. Humans have noted it since at least 1610; it was the first deep-sky object photographed, by Henry Draper in 1880.
